dataset.name: Raw soil carbon dioxide, moisture, and temperature data from a mixed conifer and aspen forest stands in the East River Watershed of Colorado June 2011-December 2021.
description: These datasets contain raw data from adjacent mixed-conifer (Abies lasiocarpa and Picea engelmannii) and deciduous (Populus tremuloides) forest stands in the Elk Mountains at the Rocky Mountain Biological Laboratory in Gothic, Colorado (38.9592◦ N, longitude: 106.9898◦ W and elevation of 2880 m). Each site contains five soil carbon dioxide (CO2) gas probes and three soil temperature/moisture sensors connected to a data logger. Soil temperature, moisture, and CO2 (ppm) concentrations were recorded each hour. There are three attached CSV files; two CSV files are of the raw data collected in the respective forest types, conifer: "Carbone_conifer.csv" and deciduous: "Carbone_aspen.csv". The third file "Carbone_Headers.csv" is a shared headers file for both datasets. Basic data processing and QA/QC was done on the raw data sets. This research was performed to investigate the response of the soil CO2 to inter-annual and seasonal variability of moisture inputs in mountainous ecosystems.

provider.name: Soil CO2 concentrations in aspen and mixed conifer forests at the Rocky Mountain Biological Laboratory in Colorado

measurementTechnique:
In 2009, two instrumented soil pits were established in adjacent stands of conifer (Abies lasiocarpa and Picea engelmannii) and deciduous (Populus tremuloides) forests in the Elk Mountains at the Rocky Mountain Biological Laboratory in Gothic, Colorado (38.9592◦ N, longitude: 106.9898◦ W and elevation of 2880 m). Soils are well-drained sandy loam superactive Ustic Haplocryolls. The mean annual temperature is 0.1oC, and the mean annual precipitation is 626 mm.
In each forest type, a soil pit was excavated with a shovel to 50 cm. At depths 50, 15, and 5 cm below the surface, soil moisture, and temperature probes (Decagon Devices 5TE, Pullman, WA, USA) were inserted horizontally in the pit sidewall. After augering holes to 50, 15, 5, and 0.5 cm depths, vertical 1” PVC pipes were inserted in the soil next to each pit and secured with metal stakes. One solid state CO2 concentration probe (Vaisala GMP222/GMM220, Vantaa Finland) and temperature sensor (thermistor, Thermometrics EC95H303W) were placed in each of the PVC pipes, as well as on a metal t-post 1.5 m above the soil surface to measure above-surface conditions. Free space in each PVC pipe was filled with closed cell foam, and the top was sealed with an elbow fitting and putty. Soil temperature, moisture, and CO2 (ppm) concentrations were recorded each hour. To eliminate heating of the soil by the soil CO2 probes and to minimize power consumption, each hour, the soil CO2 sensors were powered on for seven minutes to warm up and stabilize, then sampled every second for the next two minutes, with the average of 120 measurements recorded on the datalogger.
All CO2 concentration measurements were corrected for soil temperature and pressure according the manufacturer. Probes were calibrated annually in the field with CO2 standards, and returned to the manufacturer for factory calibration three times during the study period. For factory and field calibrations, data were corrected assuming constant linear drift over the time period between calibrations.
